heading: The week in short
body:
Pokémon's Règne Delta is out (6 November) and Mega Rayquaza ex is selling for roughly $285–$400 in English, depending on which site you trust. The 30th Celebration cards are still sliding: every special illustration rare we checked is 7–14% below its 30-day average. Dragapult ex still leads the meta at 36.5% of results, but a Slowking deck won Gdańsk on 31 October. In One Piece, OP-18 arrives on 20 November in English, and sealed Japanese OP-05 boxes are up 22% in four weeks while OP-09 and EB-02 are falling.

What to do: hold cheap 30th Celebration singles you love and don't pay launch prices for Règne Delta singles yet; wait two to four weeks. We cannot confirm the One Piece Regionals results of 7 November (see About the numbers).

heading: Règne Delta is out: Mega Rayquaza ex is the chase
body:
Méga-Évolution – Règne Delta (Delta Reign in English) went on sale on Friday 6 November. Mega Rayquaza ex comes in three versions: a Double Rare (084), a Special Illustration Rare (138) and a gold Mega Hyper Rare (141).

Early English prices disagree. Folio reports about $396 for the Special Illustration Rare and $395 for the gold card (7-day medians); Nerdsnack lists about $320 and $285; TCGindex shows about $401 for the SIR. Japanese copies of the gold card are listed at ¥50,000–¥84,800 against ¥32,000–¥34,800 for the SIR (Neokyo). There are no official pull rates; one site estimates about 1 in 480 packs for the SIR and 1 in 1,081 for the gold card, which is a guess.

Collector view: the 30th Celebration lost 10–14% a month after launch, so expect Règne Delta singles to be cheaper in two to four weeks. If you want sealed product, ask the Réunion shops now; none of the shop sites we read showed Règne Delta stock or prices.

Note: TCGdex's Cardmarket feed shows the same €5.69 for every Mega Rayquaza ex, which is clearly a placeholder, so we did not use it.

heading: 30th Celebration: still sliding, but slower
body:
The anniversary set's special illustration rares are 7–14% below their 30-day averages (Cardmarket, read 9 November): Pikachu ex 150 at €48.95 (−14%), Jirachi ex €29.53 (−14%), Mew ex 152 at €81.44 (−12%), Sylveon ex €31.04 (−11%), Gengar ex €62.51 (−10%), Salamence ex €15.18 (−10%), Mewtwo ex €45.11 (−8%). Futuristic Mew ex is at €41.84 (−7%).

From Pitch Black, Mega Darkrai ex holds at €169.56 (−2%), and Morpeko ex fell 14% to €44.67. Mew ex 152 was €78 last week, so the trend price bounced a little, but the averages are still falling.

The prices have not found a floor yet. If you want one of these for your binder, buy gradually rather than all at once.

heading: OP-18 next: English on 20 November
body:
OP-18 The Dominance of God is confirmed for 20 November in English on Bandai's product page. The Japanese date is still disputed: 21 November (Bandai page, per a reseller), 22 November (a Bandai X post) or 28 November (Japanese retail listings). We list it as unconfirmed. The set is built on Water Seven and God's Knights and has two Secret Rares drawn by Yoshitaka Amano.

French pre-release events run 21 to 28 November (€35 for 6 boosters). Miyata Kard Market in Saint-Louis showed no OP-18 listing yet; its EB-05 listing was sold out.

After the OP-17 box dropped 7% in four weeks, expect a similar settling for older sets once OP-18 opens.
source: Bandai (English products page); Samurai Sword Tokyo

heading: Sealed boxes: OP-05 up, OP-09 and EB-02 down
body:
Japanese booster-box prices (eBay sold medians, opboxindex, 9 November): OP-05 $213 (+22% in four weeks), OP-09 $109 (−23%), OP-02 $131 (−19%), EB-02 $100 (−26%), OP-01 $261 (−13%), OP-17 $116 (−7%). OP-03, OP-11, OP-15 and OP-16 are flat.

OP-05 keeps rising because fewer sealed boxes are left. If you hold older sealed boxes, OP-05 is the one with momentum. The falling ones (OP-09, EB-02) are better bought than sold right now.

The Mihawk leader ban (from 12 October) is the last big rules change we have; we found no results for the 7 November Regionals to see how the meta moved.

heading: Championships: Slowking wins Gdańsk, Dragapult still on top
body:
Regional Gdańsk (31 October, 1,739 players) was won by Aarni Karjala with Slowking. Dragapult still took four of the top 8 places. The second place was Honchkrow / Porygon2. Limitless's current deck table (format TEF-30C) puts Dragapult ex at 36.5%, Basic Box 8.9%, Slowking 7.6%, N's Zoroark ex 7.3% and Alakazam 6.4%.

The Regionals before it: Nice (17 October) Luc Gantner, Puebla (24 October) Andrew Hedrick, Louisville (10 October) Riley McKay.

One Piece: Porto and Sydney Regionals were played on 7 November. We could not find results; Limitless's One Piece page shows nothing after July. The One Piece meta shares in the dashboard are therefore last week's.

Next: Latin America Internationals (São Paulo, 20–22 November) and Regional Stuttgart (28 November).

heading: Your collection
body:
Rebuilt on 9 November: 86 of 122 cards priced (last week 95), listed value about €81.85 (last week €71.63). The two are not like-for-like because 9 fewer cards got a price this time, so don't read it as a rise or fall.

What moved: six Card 151 (JP) cards are marked Rising: Dragonite 149/165 (€6.95), Hitmonlee 107/165 (€4.06), Pikachu 025/165 (€3.72), Clefable 036/165 (€2.89), Oddish 043/165 (€2.21), Gengar 094/165 (€2.05). Dragonair 148/165 (€4.87) is the one Falling card.

What to do: your collection is worth well under €100 in total, so nothing here is worth selling for profit. Hold the Rising Card 151 cards; there is no reason to sell any card at these prices. The top card, Luffy OP15-119, is €9.82 (an English-card price used as a guide for the JP copy).

heading: Language gaps
body:
Pokémon: Règne Delta Japanese gold Mega Rayquaza is listed higher than the SIR (¥50,000–84,800 vs ¥32,000–34,800), while English prices for the two are nearly equal (about $285–$395). Compare English, French and Japanese copies again in two weeks, once French prices exist. Cardmarket pools languages into one price.

One Piece: last week we noted the Manga Rocks D. Xebec from OP-17 at about ¥436,000 in Japan against $6,100 in English. We did not re-check this week. Treat it as last week's figure.

heading: Your Réunion window: 48 days left
body:
You have 48 days on the island until 27 December. Most useful this week: ask Sortilèges, Planet Geek and Miyata Kard Market about Règne Delta and the OP-18 French release date; none of their sites showed stock or prices when we looked (Miyata had an OPK-14 Korean booster on pre-order, arrival expected 25 November). PUNK Records in Le Tampon is the One Piece specialist.

The exchange rate in the dashboard is Rs 52.95 per euro. It is not refreshed this week because valutafx.com blocked the request (403).

heading: Coming up
body: 14 Nov: One Piece Regionals in Bristol, São Paulo, Niagara Falls and Knoxville; Pokémon Special Event Buenos Aires. 20 Nov: One Piece OP-18 (EN); Pokémon Latin America Internationals (to 22 Nov). 21 Nov: Regional Oklahoma City (One Piece). 22 Nov: Champions League Chiba. 27 Nov: Pokémon Aura Seeker in Japan. 28 Nov: Regional Stuttgart (Pokémon) and Regional Alicante (One Piece). 5 Dec: Pokémon Las Vegas; One Piece Munich, Utrecht, Santiago, Mexico City. 12 Dec: One Piece Paris. 18–19 Dec: One Piece ST-37 and ST-38 starter decks.

heading: About the numbers
body: Euro prices come from Cardmarket via TCGdex; movers compare the 7-day with the 30-day average. TCGdex returned errors for part of the run and had a placeholder price for Règne Delta, so Règne Delta singles use US-dollar guides from third-party sites, which disagree. One Piece box prices are eBay sold medians in dollars from opboxindex (Japanese boxes). Unconfirmed: the OP-18 Japanese date, the 7 November One Piece Regional results, One Piece meta shares (last week's). The exchange rate was not refreshed. Collection: 86 of 122 cards priced (last week 95).
